name: Winter Haven Tree Lighting Ceremony
address: Central Park, 4th Street Northwest, Winter Haven, FL
paras: The Winter Haven community calendar lists the Annual Tree Lighting Celebration in Central Park on Thursday, December 3, from 6 PM to 7:30 PM, with no admission charge. A local Polk County holiday guide adds that live entertainment starts at 6 PM and the tree is lit at 7 PM.
Central Park sits on 4th Street Northwest in downtown Winter Haven. The same park hosts Holidays on Central two days later, so families can plan a first weekend of December around downtown.
tip: Arrive before 7 PM so the little ones are in place when the tree lights up.

name: Winter Haven Winter Wonderland
address: Central Park, 4th Street Northwest, Winter Haven, FL
paras: This free evening in Central Park runs 6 PM to 9 PM on Friday, December 11. The city calendar lists a holiday movie under the stars, inflatables to bounce on, local food trucks and holiday crafts.
Santa is available for photos from 6:30 PM to 8:30 PM, according to the host listing. Bring a blanket or chairs for the outdoor movie.
tip: Santa photos wrap up at 8:30 PM, so head to him before the movie starts.

name: Winter Haven Chain of Lakes Christmas Boat Parade
paras: Decorated boats travel from Lake May to Lake Howard, back to Lake May, then onto Lake Shipp on Saturday, December 5, starting promptly at 6:30 PM, based on the Visit Central Florida listing.

The listing names four waterfront spots for watching: Harborside Restaurant, Tanner's Lakeside Bar and Grill, Old Man Franks and the Twisted Prop. It does not give street addresses, so check each venue before you go.
tip: Waterfront restaurants are the listed viewing spots, so book a table or arrive early.

name: Havendale Christmas Parade
address: Havendale Blvd NW, Winter Haven, FL
paras: The Havendale Christmas Parade rolls on Friday, December 4, from 7 PM to 9 PM. The listing describes a route of about 3.1 miles along Havendale Boulevard, starting near 14th Street and heading west toward Auburndale, ending just before 42nd Street.
The $50 per unit fee on the listing is the parade entry registration for floats and groups, not a charge for watching from the roadside.
tip: Pick a spot along Havendale Boulevard and bring layers for the evening.
